title: Severe cyclonic storm makes landfall on the Odisha coast
text: Early-warning systems and pre-emptive evacuation kept casualties in single digits, but crop losses across four coastal districts are still being assessed. The storm crossed the coast near Paradip with sustained winds of about 120 km/h. The state evacuated nearly three lakh people to cyclone shelters over 36 hours. Cyclones in the North Indian Ocean are named from a list contributed by WMO/ESCAP Panel member countries. IMD classifies a “severe cyclonic storm” at 89–117 km/h sustained winds.

title: Analysis: Severe cyclonic storm makes landfall on the Odisha coast
text: Odisha’s “zero-casualty” model is cited as a benchmark for disaster governance under the Sendai Framework. Warmer Bay of Bengal surface waters are linked to faster intensification. NDMA is chaired by the Prime Minister under the Disaster Management Act, 2005. Timeline: 24 Sep - Low-pressure area forms over central Bay of Bengal; 26 Sep - IMD issues orange alert for Odisha, Andhra Pradesh; 27 Sep - Evacuation of coastal blocks begins; 28 Sep - Landfall near Paradip.

title: Constitution Bench sets outer limits on Governor’s time to act on State Bills
text: The ruling reads a “reasonable time” requirement into Article 200 and holds that indefinite withholding of assent is not constitutionally permissible. A five-judge bench held that a Governor must act on a Bill within a reasonable period and cannot sit on it indefinitely. The Court said reserved Bills should ordinarily be decided by the President within three months. Article 200 lists the Governor’s options: assent, withhold, return (non-Money Bills) or reserve for the President. Article 201 governs Bills reserved for the President’s consideration.

title: Analysis: Constitution Bench sets outer limits on Governor’s time to act on State Bills
text: The verdict addresses a recurring Centre–State friction point and is expected to shape cooperative federalism debates. It builds on earlier rulings on gubernatorial discretion. Article 163 deals with the Council of Ministers aiding and advising the Governor. Timeline: Mar 2026 - State moves SC over pending Bills; Jul 2026 - Reference to five-judge bench; 26 Sep - Judgment delivered.

title: ISRO completes second uncrewed orbital test ahead of crewed mission
text: The crew module, carrying a humanoid payload, splashed down in the Bay of Bengal after validating life-support and re-entry systems. The uncrewed flight orbited for three days before a controlled re-entry and sea recovery. Telemetry confirmed nominal performance of the environmental control system. The crew module is designed for a low-Earth orbit of about 400 km. The Crew Escape System is tested separately via Test Vehicle missions.

title: Analysis: ISRO completes second uncrewed orbital test ahead of crewed mission
text: A successful test keeps India on track to become the fourth nation to independently send humans to orbit. Most subsystems were developed domestically. IN-SPACe authorises and promotes private participation in space activities. Timeline: 21 Sep - Launch from Sriharikota; 24 Sep - Re-entry and splashdown; 25 Sep - Module recovered by Navy.

title: Parliament clears amendment to the data protection law
text: Changes tighten rules on children’s data and expand the Data Protection Board’s powers to impose penalties. Both Houses passed the amendment by voice vote after a short debate. The Board can now initiate inquiries suo motu in specified cases. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act was enacted in 2023. The Data Protection Board is established by the Central Government.

title: Analysis: Parliament clears amendment to the data protection law
text: Critics argue the Board’s independence remains limited as members are appointed by the Union government. The right to privacy was recognised in the Puttaswamy judgment (2017). Timeline: Aug 2026 - Bill introduced in Lok Sabha; 18 Sep - Passed by Lok Sabha; 22 Sep - Passed by Rajya Sabha.

title: India and the EU announce conclusion of free trade agreement talks
text: The deal covers goods, services and investment protection, with a separate chapter on trade and sustainable development. Negotiators closed the remaining chapters after nearly a decade of on-off talks. Tariffs on most industrial goods will be phased out over ten years. The EU is among India’s largest trading partners in goods. CBAM initially covers iron & steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen.

title: Analysis: India and the EU announce conclusion of free trade agreement talks
text: The EU’s carbon border mechanism remains outside the agreement and could affect Indian steel exports. Talks on the India–EU BTIA first began in 2007. Timeline: 2007 - BTIA negotiations launched; 2022 - Talks relaunched; 19 Sep - Conclusion announced.

title: Intersessional climate talks agree draft text on adaptation finance
text: Developing countries pushed for a quantified adaptation goal; the draft leaves the final number for ministers to decide. Parties agreed a negotiating text with bracketed options on adaptation finance. India argued for grant-based finance over loans. The Paris Agreement’s Global Goal on Adaptation is in Article 7. The Ramsar Convention concerns wetlands of international importance.

title: Analysis: Intersessional climate talks agree draft text on adaptation finance
text: Adaptation funding remains a fraction of mitigation finance, a gap highlighted by vulnerable nations. CITES regulates international trade in endangered species. Timeline: 8 Sep - Session opens; 17 Sep - Draft text agreed.

title: RBI holds repo rate, nudges growth forecast upward
text: The Monetary Policy Committee voted 5–1 to keep rates unchanged while retaining a neutral stance. The policy repo rate was held steady. The growth projection for the year was revised up by 20 basis points. The MPC has six members: three from RBI and three appointed by the Government. The inflation target is 4% CPI with a ±2% band.

title: Analysis: RBI holds repo rate
text: Food inflation has eased but core inflation remains sticky, limiting room for cuts. The MPC was constituted under the amended RBI Act, 1934. Timeline: 13 Sep - MPC meeting begins; 15 Sep - Decision announced.

title: Census house-listing begins, with caste enumeration in the next phase
text: The first digital census will allow self-enumeration through a mobile application. Enumerators began house-listing operations in the first batch of states. Caste data will be collected during population enumeration. Census is a Union List subject (Entry 69). The Census Act was enacted in 1948.

title: Analysis: Census house-listing begins
text: Updated data will inform delimitation, welfare targeting and urban planning. The last full census was conducted in 2011. Timeline: Jun 2026 - Notification issued; 12 Sep - House-listing begins.

title: Cabinet extends school meal scheme to pre-primary classes
text: Breakfast will be piloted in aspirational districts, adding an estimated 1.2 crore children. The Union Cabinet approved coverage of Balvatika children under the scheme. A breakfast pilot will run in 112 districts. PM-POSHAN was earlier known as the Mid-Day Meal Scheme. It is a centrally sponsored scheme.

title: Analysis: Cabinet extends school meal scheme to pre-primary classes
text: Evidence links school meals to enrolment, attendance and nutrition outcomes. NFSA, 2013 provides a legal entitlement to school meals. Timeline: 10 Sep - Cabinet approval.

title: Magnitude 5.8 earthquake strikes Assam–Bhutan border region
text: Tremors were felt across the Northeast; minor structural damage reported in two districts. The quake struck at a shallow depth of about 10 km. No casualties were reported. Seismic Zone V covers the entire Northeast. The National Center for Seismology is under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

title: Analysis: Magnitude 5.8 earthquake strikes Assam–Bhutan border region
text: The region lies in Seismic Zone V, the highest-risk category. Shallow-focus quakes generally cause stronger surface shaking. Timeline: 6 Sep - Earthquake recorded; 7 Sep - Aftershocks of M3–4.

title: Market regulator bars auditor over lapses in listed-company fraud
text: The order finds the audit firm ignored repeated red flags on related-party transactions. The regulator barred the audit firm from listed-company work for two years. It found partners failed to exercise professional scepticism. NFRA oversees auditing standards for listed and large companies. Related-party transactions require audit committee approval under the Companies Act.

title: Analysis: Market regulator bars auditor over lapses in listed-company fraud
text: The case raises questions of auditor independence and gatekeeper accountability. Auditor rotation is mandated for listed companies. Timeline: 2024 - Fraud surfaces; 3 Sep - Final order issued.

title: Delimitation commission notified, clearing the path for women’s reservation
text: Seats reserved for women will take effect after delimitation based on the new census. The government notified the commission’s composition. Its work will begin after census figures are published. The 106th Amendment reserves one-third of seats for women in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies. Delimitation orders cannot be challenged in court.

title: Analysis: Delimitation commission notified
text: The sequencing has been criticised for delaying implementation. Article 82 provides for readjustment after each census. Timeline: Sep 2023 - 106th Amendment enacted; 29 Aug - Commission notified.
